wikipedia.title: Kayamkulam
wikipedia.text:
Kayamkulam (IPA: [kaːjɐmkuɭam, kaːjɐŋɡuɭam]) is a municipality in the Alappuzha district of Kerala, India. It is located 45 km (28.0 mi) south of the district headquarters in Alappuzha and about 107 km (66.5 mi) north of the state capital Thiruvananthapuram. As per the 2011 Indian census, Kayamkulam has a population of 68,634 people, and a population density of 3,149/km2 (8,160/sq mi).
Kayamkulam was the erstwhile capital of the Kingdom of Onattukara, and today continues to be the largest town in the Onattukara region.

wikipedia.text: Kappil is a small village in Alappuzha district of Kerala state, India.

wikipedia.title: Keerikkad
wikipedia.text: Keerikkad (Town) is a suburban region in Alappuzha district in the Indian state of Kerala. There are two major attractions in Keerikkad. One is Evoor Sree Krishna Swamy temple and Ramapuram Bhagavathi Temple. Lord Krishna is the main deity of the former temple while Ma Kali is the main deity of the latter.

wikipedia.title: Kayamkulam Junction railway station
wikipedia.text: Kayamkulam Junction railway station (station code: KYJ) is an NSG–3 category Indian railway station in Thiruvananthapuram railway division of Southern Railway zone.. It stands at the junction of three lines- south towards Thiruvananthapuram via Kollam, north towards Ernakulam via Alappuzha and north-east towards Ernakulam Junction/Ernakulam Town via Kottayam. The station is  located 1.7 km (1.1 mi) from Kayamkulam in Alappuzha district of Kerala, near the Kayamkulam–Pathanapuram Road also known as KP road. In 2018, the rail wi-fi broad-band connection has been introduced in Kayamkulam.

wikivoyage.title: Kayamkulam
wikivoyage.text:
Kayamkulam is a city and a municipality in district of the Indian state of Kerala. It is an ancient maritime trading centre and is almost equidistant from Alappuzha town and Kollam.


== See ==
Oachira Vrishchikam festival is celebrated every year at the Oachira Temple.
Chettikulangara Kumbha Bharani, the Bharani festival celebrated in the month of Kumbham is an important event for the people of this locality and neighbouring places.

1 Krishnapuram Palace, Oachira Rd (Along NH-47, between Kayamkulam town and Oachira), ☏ +91 479 244 1133. Palace and museum with exhibits about the Travancore kingdom. The palace was built during the 18th century by Travancore Maharaja Marthanda Varma. (updated Jul 2020)
